steps.scene: You're on a slip road joining a busy motorway. The left-hand lane is full of traffic doing about 60 mph.

options.text: Stop at the end of the slip road and wait for a big gap
Match your speed to the left lane and filter into a safe gap
Carry on along the hard shoulder until a gap appears

question.explanation: Traffic on the motorway has priority. The slip road is there so you can reach its speed and slot in without making anyone brake.

steps.title: Joining, step by step
steps.prompt: Put joining a motorway in order, from the start of the slip road.

items.text: Look early at the traffic already in the left-hand lane
Use the slip road to match that traffic's speed
Merge into a safe gap in the left-hand lane
Stay in the left-hand lane while you get used to the speed

steps.explanation: Look, match, merge, settle. Never force your way in — adjust your speed until the gap is safe.

steps.title: Settle in before you overtake
steps.body: Once you've joined, stay in the left-hand lane long enough to get used to the speed of the traffic before you think about overtaking.

question.prompt: You've just merged from the slip road. What's your next move?

options.text: Move out a lane so you're not stuck behind lorries
Readjust your mirrors for motorway driving
Stay in the left-hand lane for a while

question.explanation: Motorway speeds feel different at first. Give yourself time in the left lane to judge them before you change lanes.

a.label: Single carriageway
a.body: National speed limit for a car: 60 mph.

b.label: Dual carriageway or motorway
b.body: National speed limit for a car: 70 mph.

question.prompt: You pass a national speed limit sign as you join the motorway. How fast may your car go?

options.text: 60 mph, the same as any open road
There isn't one — you choose a safe speed

question.explanation: 70 mph on motorways and dual carriageways, 60 mph on single carriageways — unless signs show a lower limit.

steps.scene: You're cruising at 70 mph in light traffic. Everything around you looks calm and steady.

question.prompt: Where should most of your attention be?

options.text: Much further ahead than you'd look on slower roads
On the car right in front — that's the one you could hit
On your speedometer, to hold exactly 70

question.explanation: At motorway speed a hazard reaches you far sooner. Looking well ahead gives you time to react to it.

steps.title: Your gap at 70 mph
steps.body: Leave at least a two-second gap to the vehicle ahead — at least double that on a wet road. At motorway speed, that gap is your only thinking time.

question.prompt: It's raining hard on the motorway. What gap should you leave?

options.text: Two seconds, the same as on a dry road
Whatever gap the traffic around you is leaving

question.explanation: Stopping distances at least double in the wet, so your gap must at least double too.

steps.wrongBelief: Any vehicle that's legal on the road is allowed on a motorway.

question.prompt: Which of these must not use a motorway?

options.text: None of them — if it's road legal, it can go on

question.explanation: Motorways are for fast traffic. Slow or vulnerable users are kept off them.

steps.repairNote: Pedestrians, cyclists, horse riders, motorcycles under 50 cc and mobility scooters are among those banned.
